# Log Entry \#4

# Week of February 25-March 4

This week, I mainly just recreated the datamoshing effect.   
The result can be seen below.  
[Datamosh Demo](https://youtu.be/AHOuCyrbUOc)   
I still need to tweak it and test it with a headset because there is some weird zooming that’s happening.

I plan to create a triggerable bitcrushing effect for audio and a few simple visual glitches like blocky lines that appear in and out which will have multiple parameters that can be manipulated to allow the user to engage with the act.

For the hologram, I plan to create effects that will only reveal certain aspects of the model (like just certain maps in the material).

The show and tell from this week gave me some insight into how people see glitches. Someone replied saying that a simulated glitch is indistinguishable from a real glitch and someone else says that the difference is predictability. Both have the same idea, the strengths and the weaknesses of my glitches will depend on my interaction system. It makes me more comfortable simulating most of my glitches and any real glitches will be a nice bonus caused by my developer oversights.

My show and tell also let me determine the deliverables for a worst case scenario, which will be a gallery-style experience that showcases the glitch effects. One person had a good question which is how will I maintain the attention of the audience and what will the interactive elements be. I think I will take inspiration from Radiohead’s *Kid Amnesia* experience: a digital museum dedicated to the *Kid A* and *Amnesiac* albums. Each song has a certain room/space dedicated to it, each with a unique setting. I plan to do something similar by perhaps creating individual rooms for each glitch (this could be too big to let the user physically walk around like in the original plan).

My plan for the couple of weeks before spring break is to write the scripts for game elements to trigger the glitch effects. I will need to pick up the pace if I want to get the MVP done by spring break.
